control.label: Control
control.summary: You control a country when your influence is at least its Stability and exceeds the opponent's influence by at least that Stability.
control.example: Stability 3: your 4 vs their 2 is not control. Increasing yours to 5 gives a lead of 3 and control.

influence.label: Influence
influence.summary: Influence represents political investment in a country. Both sides can have influence; having it does not necessarily mean control.
influence.example: Adding 1 influence normally costs 1 Operation, or 2 in an enemy-controlled country.

stability.label: Stability
stability.summary: The country's fixed threshold for control, also used to calculate coup difficulty.
stability.example: Stability 3 requires an influence lead of 3 to control; a coup subtracts 2 × 3 from its total.

battleground.label: Battleground
battleground.summary: A specially marked strategic country. Battlegrounds affect regional scoring; coups there normally lower DEFCON.
battleground.example: Each controlled battleground normally adds 1 VP. The map badge identifies battleground status.

ordinary.label: Non-battleground
ordinary.summary: An ordinary country without a battleground marker. It still counts toward the regional country total.
ordinary.example: Domination requires at least one controlled non-battleground in addition to a battleground advantage.

coup.label: Coup
coup.summary: Choose a legal target with enemy influence. Die + Operations − 2 × Stability gives the influence change if positive.
coup.example: Die 5 + Operations 2 − Stability 2 × 2 = 3. Remove 2 enemy influence first; the remaining 1 becomes yours.

realignment.label: Realignment
realignment.summary: Costs 1 Operation per roll. Both sides roll with modifiers; the higher total removes enemy influence equal to the difference. It never adds your influence.
realignment.example: Controlled neighbors, influence advantage and an adjacent friendly superpower modify rolls. A final 6 vs 4 removes 2 from the loser.

defcon.label: DEFCON
defcon.summary: This game's nuclear crisis ranges from 5 (peaceful) to 2 (critical). It never falls below 2, preventing sudden losses to nuclear war.
defcon.example: At 2, coups that would cause nuclear war cannot be selected. Safe non-battleground coups remain available, subject to regional restrictions.

milops.label: Military Operations
milops.summary: Each turn requires military activity. Coups and war events provide Military Operations; realignments do not.
milops.example: At turn end, if 3 are required and you completed 1, the opponent gains the 2 VP difference.

required-milops.label: Required Military Operations
required-milops.summary: At turn end, the military requirement equals the current DEFCON level.
required-milops.example: Required 3, completed 1: shortfall 2. Exceeding the requirement earns no extra VP.

headline.label: Headline Phase
headline.summary: Before the turn's actions, both players secretly choose a card, reveal together, and resolve both events.
headline.example: Higher Operations resolves first; the US wins ties. Scoring cards count as 0; the China Card cannot be a headline.

action-round.label: Action Round
action-round.summary: One side plays a card and resolves all its events or Operations before the other side acts.
action-round.example: Normally the USSR acts first, then the US: 6 actions each in early war and 7 in mid/late war.

turn.label: Turn
turn.summary: A turn contains dealing, headlines, multiple action rounds and end-of-turn checks.
turn.example: This turn lasts until the current turn ends; this action round covers only the current side's action.

ops.label: Operations
ops.summary: The upper-left card value. Choose one use: influence placement, realignment, coup or the Space Race.
ops.example: 3 Operations normally place 3 total influence in countries not controlled by the enemy. Event Operations follow their card text.

vp.label: Victory Points
vp.summary: Both sides share one VP track. Gaining VP moves the marker toward your side.
vp.example: The US gaining 2 moves the marker 2 toward the US. Either side reaching 20 VP wins immediately.

scoring.label: Scoring
scoring.summary: Compare controlled countries in a region, then award the card's Presence, Domination or Control value.
scoring.example: Usually add battleground and enemy-superpower adjacency points. The difference moves the VP marker.

scoring-card.label: Scoring card
scoring-card.summary: Scores its region directly and has no Operations. When only enough actions remain, only highlighted scoring cards may be played.
scoring-card.example: Two actions left with two scoring cards: other cards are locked until you play the scoring cards.

non-scoring-card.label: Non-scoring card
non-scoring-card.summary: Any card other than a regional scoring card. Effects asking for one exclude scoring cards.
non-scoring-card.example: With a 3-Operations event and Europe Scoring, only the event is eligible.

presence.label: Presence
presence.summary: The basic regional scoring threshold: control at least one country in the region.
presence.example: Influence without control of any country does not qualify.

domination.label: Domination
domination.summary: Control more total countries and more battlegrounds than your opponent, including at least one battleground and one non-battleground.
domination.example: A battleground lead alone is insufficient; all three conditions must be met.

region-control.label: Regional Control
region-control.summary: Control more countries than the opponent and every battleground in the region.
region-control.example: This is a regional scoring status, distinct from controlling one country. European Control wins immediately.

final-scoring.label: Final Scoring
final-scoring.summary: After turn 10, score the six main regions and award 1 VP to the China Card's holder.
final-scoring.example: Southeast Asia is not scored separately. Compare final VP; a level track is a draw.

space.label: Space Race
space.summary: Use a card meeting the next space's Operations requirement, then roll within its success range to advance.
space.example: Normally one attempt per turn. Space cards never trigger their event, even an opposing event.

hand.label: Hand
hand.summary: Cards you hold and have not played, normally hidden from your opponent. Refill to 8 in early war, 9 later.
hand.example: The China Card is separate and does not count toward this limit. Scoring cards cannot be held across turns.

deck.label: Draw pile
deck.summary: Undrawn cards lie face down. When empty, the discard pile is normally reshuffled into a new deck.
deck.example: Removed cards never return. Mid- and late-war cards enter on their designated turns.

draw.label: Draw
draw.summary: Take cards from the draw pile into your hand, as specified by the rules or an event.
draw.example: Drawing does not trigger a card's event; playing or another effect does.

discard-pile.label: Discard pile
discard-pile.summary: Used or discarded cards that have not been permanently removed lie here face up.
discard-pile.example: They may be reshuffled when the draw pile empties. Starred cards are normally removed only after their event triggers.

discard.label: Discard
discard.summary: Move a specified card from your hand to the discard pile. Forced discards do not trigger the discarded event.
discard.example: Discarding differs from playing for Operations, which may trigger an opposing event.

removed.label: Removed from play
removed.summary: Starred events are normally permanently removed once their event actually triggers. They are not reshuffled.
removed.example: Using your own card only for Operations does not trigger its event. Unmet prerequisites do not automatically remove a starred card.

draft-tension.label: Tension
draft-tension.summary: A situation meter from the old concept deck, modified by that deck's card text.
draft-tension.example: This prototype term is distinct from the current deck's DEFCON.

draft-prestige.label: Prestige
draft-prestige.summary: A scoring resource from the old concept deck, gained or lost as instructed.
draft-prestige.example: The current deck uses Victory Points; Prestige remains only in the separate prototype.

draft-tally.label: Tally
draft-tally.summary: The old concept deck's instruction to calculate a region's result.
draft-tally.example: The current deck uses Scoring. Prototype values follow its own draft rules.
